question: What operator price (opening and closing) exists for each Week 11 market, with a timestamp we can verify?
why_it_blocks_decisions: Without a verified market line there is no residual, no CLV, and no benchmark-relative skill score; the leaderboard cannot rank anything.
information_needed: Opening and closing prices per market per game from a named operator with an auditable timestamp.
where_to_get_it_officially: Sportsbook pages are not reachable or auditable from this sandbox; a licensed-operator API or an archived quote feed reviewed against the operator's terms is required.
notes: NFL publishes its sportsbook partners; the partner list is official but the prices are not. Flag F-P01 blocks all market columns.

question: Are official NFL Game Books available per 2026 week from this sandbox, and at what URL pattern?
why_it_blocks_decisions: R044 requires actual starters and game-day status from Game Books only; without them the availability graph (R029) cannot be built on official evidence.
information_needed: A confirmed per-week Game Book PDF URL pattern (or an explicit statement that they are not accessible from here).
where_to_get_it_officially: https://nflcomms.blob.core.windows.net/ or operations.nfl.com game-book indices - to be probed and recorded per week.
notes: No Game Book URL has been verified from this sandbox yet; none are asserted anywhere in this desk.

question: Which official source carries per-game inactive lists and snap shares for 2026?
why_it_blocks_decisions: R049/R065 need the active list and snap share per player per game; without them a backup replacing a starter can be suspected but not confirmed.
information_needed: A published inactive-list source and a snap-count source with per-game rows.
where_to_get_it_officially: NFL.com inactives articles exist weekly (week-9 inactives article seen on the injury page); snap counts would need an official or officially-licensed feed.
notes: Inactives articles were observed on the official injury page news block (2026-11-18 read); they are not yet structured data.

question: When will the Week 11 official injury report be published, and does reg11 serve it on request?
why_it_blocks_decisions: F-P02: at the 2026-11-18 read the reg11 URL served Week 10 content; Week 11 availability cannot enter any model until captured.
information_needed: A successful reg11 fetch returning Week 11 tables, with the read timestamp.
where_to_get_it_officially: https://www.nfl.com/injuries/league/2026/reg11 (re-read daily Wed-Fri per the snapshot suggestion).
notes: Requested URL reg11 served reg10 content at 2026-11-18T03:55:13Z; the request-vs-served mismatch is itself flagged (F-P03).

question: Is the one-pass HFA estimate (-0.288 points, n=142) stable, or is it an artefact of unbalanced home/away counts so far?
why_it_blocks_decisions: The sign of HFA flips several Week 11 fair spreads; decisions that depend on small edges need to know whether HFA is estimable at all this season.
information_needed: More weeks of data and/or a pre-registered bootstrap interval for HFA; also a comparison against a home/away-split rating.
where_to_get_it_officially: Re-run the frozen spec weekly as results accrue (the pipeline is deterministic and re-derives everything).
notes: HFA is published with n and the limitation is stated; no interval is asserted yet.

question: Do the printed injury-report anomalies (Kenneth Walker III listed under KC, Myles Garrett LB under LAR, Mike Evans under SF) reflect real 2026 roster moves or page defects?
why_it_blocks_decisions: R052 treats roster turnover as a first-class data event; misattribution would corrupt any availability feature built from these rows.
information_needed: Per-club official roster or transaction pages for the affected players, read and stored with timestamps.
where_to_get_it_officially: Club transaction/roster pages on nfl.com or club sites; the transactions log referenced by earlier desks (VR-17/VR-26).
notes: Rows are recorded verbatim as printed and flagged (F-P04); no interpretation is published.

question: What is the sanctioned way to store raw capture bytes so hashes cover server responses rather than extracts?
why_it_blocks_decisions: F-P09: extract-level hashes cannot prove server content; an auditor cannot replay the exact bytes.
information_needed: Either a fetcher allowed to retain raw HTML in-repo (size permitting) or an external immutable store with retention terms accepted.
where_to_get_it_officially: Legal/terms review of nfl.com terms plus a storage decision; earlier desks left this to a terms review.
notes: Inherited from F-09 (3cb7800c); unresolved by this desk by design.

question: Which single source of record settles club-code conflicts (AZ/LA vs ARI/LAR) across official pages?
why_it_blocks_decisions: Team joins silently break on these aliases; every cross-source join needs one canonical mapping.
information_needed: A documented alias table accepted repo-wide, or confirmation that nfl.com publishes a canonical abbreviation list.
where_to_get_it_officially: operations.nfl.com media guides record official abbreviations; to be verified before any change to existing desks' data.
notes: This desk normalizes to the pinned nflverse codes and records both printed forms in raw extracts.

question: Should Week 11 totals receive a partial HFA term, given the spec currently applies HFA to spreads only?
why_it_blocks_decisions: The pre-registered spec excludes HFA from totals (documented simplification); if HFA materially shifts totals, the policy needs a pre-registered revision, not an edit.
information_needed: A walk-forward comparison of totals with and without an HFA term over multiple seasons (R070-style two-estimator publication).
where_to_get_it_officially: Historical weekly totals from official results; the comparison must be pre-registered before looking.
notes: Any change goes through a new spec version and a new snapshot, never an in-place edit.

question: Who owns the scheduled (daily Wed-Fri) capture job for availability snapshots?
why_it_blocks_decisions: R047/R048 need automation; two stamped reads exist but nothing schedules the next one.
information_needed: A maintained scheduled workflow with an owner session and alerting on drift.
where_to_get_it_officially: GitHub Actions scheduled workflow writing to an agreed snapshot directory; owner to be claimed in COORDINATION.md.
notes: Suggestion S-P03 proposes the design; it is published for review, not implemented unilaterally across namespaces.
